executive_summary:
**Where Qnet actually is.** This is a mature, unusually disciplined codebase with a commercial-grade *substrate* and a commercial-grade *gap*. The substrate is real and must not be rebuilt: Figma-class smart alignment guides with per-axis grid arbitration and live ⌃-suspend (CanvasGeometry.swift:1184-1330, NetworkCanvasView.swift:558-621); ⌥-drag duplicate-and-move committed as ONE undo step (NetworkCanvasScrollContainer.swift:443-467); snapshot undo that captures the four auto-naming counters (NetworkEditorModel.swift:2241-2355); a single-owner cursor with no push/pop (NetworkCanvasScrollContainer.swift:722-782); a terminal whose host NSView is cached and re-parented so no layout change can restart the shell (TerminalConsoleView.swift:570-620); run cancellation that signals the process *group* and escalates SIGINT→SIGTERM→SIGKILL (TerminalModel.swift:624-691); a design system enforced by a lint that generates its own forbidden-symbol alternation from the tokens (validation/design_lint.sh:216-238); and source-text contracts that pin the solver-launch wrapper (validation/gui_runtime_contracts.sh).

The gap is that almost none of the *product* layer on top of that substrate has been finished. I verified each of the following myself:

1. **Universal decimal places is a lie the Settings pane tells.** `appSettings.outputDecimals` is read at exactly ONE place in 64k lines — QnetGUIApp.swift:5298 — feeding the comparison awk. 10 of the 22 run paths (every Python solver, MLMC, LP) print raw solver prose at 4/6/8/9/10/12/17 significant digits, and the Results workspace has three copies of `significantDigits(1...7)` (ResultsWorkspace.swift:1513/1769/1949) that never consult the setting. One number, four precisions, one screen.

2. **The canvas cannot express the model it exists to draw.** Delete on a selected link is a dead no-op with an *enabled* menu item (NetworkEditorModel.swift:680-682 guards on node ids only); a self-loop is flatly refused (`"Cannot link a node to itself."`, NetworkEditorModel.swift:1982-1986) although the renderer already draws one (CanvasGeometry.swift:343-370) and the exporters already report them; drag-from-node-to-node is a silent no-op (NetworkCanvasView.swift:466-470 returns for every tool but `.select`/`.multiSelect`); and the double-click the user explicitly asked for has no branch at all (NetworkCanvasView.swift:744-749), while in an add tool it silently stacks two nodes on one grid point.

3. **There is no way to start.** `grep -riE 'archetype|template|preset'` across Sources/Qnet returns nothing. The empty canvas is a `DSEmptyState` with `.allowsHitTesting(false)` on the whole view (NetworkCanvasOverlays.swift:161-171) even though DSEmptyState already supports an action button (DSEmptyState.swift:29-31, 80-92). The 50 bundled examples the File menu promises are **not in the app**: `find Qnet.app -name '*.bnet'` returns 0, and `findExamplesDirectory` walks up only from the process CWD (QnetGUIApp.swift:1421-1435) — for a Finder launch that is `/`. And a hand-built network is born exactly critical: source and station both default to `rate=1.0`, so ρ = 1.000 (Models.swift:207, NetworkEditorModel.swift:2106).

4. **Nothing pops out and nothing that edits can be moved.** `grep -riE 'detach|undock|pop ?out|tear.?off'` returns only `Task.detached`. All 11 `.sheet(` presentations are pinned to the parent window, plus one hand-rolled `NSWindow`+`beginSheet` (CanvasExportOptionsSheet.swift:184-197) and 87 app-modal `showAlert(` calls in QnetGUIApp alone. Five auxiliary windows call `setFrameAutosaveName` but never `setFrameUsingName`, and `AuxiliaryWindow.make` ends with an unconditional `window.center()` (WindowSupport.swift:125) — so the frame never comes back.

5. **The shell is architecturally the centrepiece and presentationally the footer.** It shares the bottom row with the AI pane at an ideal height of 248 pt against the canvas row's 520, the Results pane force-shows itself on the first run and never stops (ContentView.swift:319-325), `⌘F` with the shell focused opens the *canvas* Find Node dialog (`case .shell, .canvas: actions.findNode()`, QnetCommands.swift:625-627) while three surfaces advertise otherwise, `⌘C` is disabled for a terminal selection (QnetCommands.swift:387), there is no right-click menu, and the width-measurement mechanism that stops wide tables wrapping has exactly two callers, both Swift-generated reports (QnetGUIApp.swift:6070, 6125) — no solver run ever feeds it.

Round 1 ships the five things the user named, plus the one integrity fix behind them.

workstreams.name: Canvas gestures and rendering (view layer only)
workstreams.mission: Make the canvas surface behave the way a commercial diagram editor behaves: the pointer modes the user named, drag-to-connect with an elastic preview, an actionable empty state, and correct chrome geometry. W1 owns the VIEW layer only — it never edits NetworkEditorModel.swift. The model API it needs (`pendingLinkPoint`, `enterStickyPan()`, `exitStickyPan()`, `toolBeforeStickyPan`, `pendingFitOnAppear`) is landed by the integrator's pre-round seed, so W1 compiles independently of W2.

tasks.title: Sticky pan: double-click empty canvas becomes the hand, a single click returns the pointer
tasks.rationale: Named verbatim by the user. Today a double-click on empty canvas does nothing in the Pointer tool (two deselects) and, worse, in an add tool it silently places TWO nodes at the same snapped grid point — the second invisible under the first, quietly corrupting the network. VERIFIED: the empty-canvas onEnded at NetworkCanvasView.swift:744-749 calls editor.handleCanvasTap unconditionally with no double-click branch, while the node path (NetworkCanvasView.swift:517-528) and the link path (:721-728) BOTH already implement double-click against NSEvent.doubleClickInterval — the pattern to copy is in this very file. handleCanvasTap (NetworkEditorModel.swift:402-427) places a node on every tap for the four add tools, which is the double-placement.
tasks.implementation: Add `@State private var lastCanvasTapTime: Date` and `@State private var lastCanvasTapPoint: CGPoint?` to CanvasContentView, mirroring lastNodeTapTime/lastLinkTapTime at NetworkCanvasView.swift:177-191. In the empty-canvas onEnded branch (NetworkCanvasView.swift:744-749): when the tool is .select or .multiSelect and the second click lands within Self.doubleClickInterval AND within 3 pt of the first (tighter than the 5-pt marquee threshold at :198), call `editor.enterStickyPan()` instead of handleCanvasTap. When the tool is .pan and `editor.toolBeforeStickyPan != nil`, call `editor.exitStickyPan()` instead of handleCanvasTap — a Pan-tool click already routes to this branch. When the tool is one of the four add tools, suppress the second placement: require the tap to be outside the double-click window OR at a different snapped point. THE CURSOR NEEDS NO WORK: the clip view is the sole cursor owner, already subscribes to $selectedTool (NetworkCanvasScrollContainer.swift:170-184), and cursorForCurrentState() already returns .openHand for .pan and .closedHand while isPanningCanvas (VERIFIED at :731-751). Correct the two doc comments that currently assert the opposite rule (NetworkCanvasView.swift:39-40 and :768-770) and add the gesture to KeyboardShortcutReference.unprintedKeys (:139-151).
tasks.acceptance_criteria: Pointer tool, double-click empty canvas: the cursor becomes an open hand, the status bar's tool segment reads "Pan", dragging pans. A single click anywhere returns the tool to Pointer and the cursor to the arrow. H and the palette still work and are unaffected by the memo. With the Station tool, a fast double-click on empty canvas places exactly ONE station (verify with the status-bar primitive count). The gesture appears under "KEYS NOT PRINTED IN A MENU" in Help ▸ Keyboard Shortcuts. swift build and validation/design_lint.sh pass.

Escape must still mean Deselect All (NetworkCanvasScrollContainer.swift:606-610).

tasks.title: Drag from node to node creates a link, with an elastic rubber-band preview
tasks.rationale: Drag-to-connect is the universal way to draw an arc in Visio, OmniGraffle, Simulink, yEd and Figma. VERIFIED it is a silent no-op here: nodeDrag's onChanged returns immediately unless the tool is .select or .multiSelect (NetworkCanvasView.swift:466-470), so dragNodeID stays nil, and onEnded therefore takes the plain-click path with the PRESS node — the release target is never consulted. Even the two-click fallback has no elastic line: pendingLinkIndicator (NetworkCanvasView.swift:319-339, VERIFIED) draws only a dashed outline ring around the start node, so the user cannot see what they are about to connect.
tasks.implementation: (1) In nodeDrag.onChanged add an `.addLink` branch: once CanvasMath.length(value.translation) crosses Self.dragThreshold, set `editor.pendingLinkStartID = node.id` and publish the live pointer position into the pre-seeded `editor.pendingLinkPoint`. In nodeDrag.onEnded, when a link drag is in flight, hit-test the release location with `scene.hitNode(at:)` and call the existing internal `editor.handleLinkSelection(targetID)` so the class-selection, duplicate-pair and chain-continuation rules are byte-identical to the two-click path; release on empty canvas clears pendingLinkStartID and pendingLinkPoint. The `.node` early-return in the canvas-level drag (NetworkCanvasView.swift:658-661) must keep the canvas gesture out of the way. (2) Extend pendingLinkIndicator (:319-339) to also stroke a dashed path from the start node's boundary to `editor.pendingLinkPoint` — or to the hovered node's boundary when one is under the pointer — reusing the `chainColor` it already computes and the sanctioned `StrokeStyle(lineWidth: max(1.5, 2 * s), dash: [...])` spelling already at :330-334. `.allowsHitTesting(false)` and `.accessibilityHidden(true)`. (3) Feed pendingLinkPoint from the existing updateHover tracker (:434-461) so the two-click flow gets the same preview with no extra event plumbing and no new per-frame publish path.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: Link tool: press on S1 and drag — a dashed accent line follows the pointer; hover S2 — the line snaps to S2's boundary and S2 shows its hover ring; release — the link is created and the status log prints the same "Linked …" line the two-click flow prints. Releasing on empty canvas leaves no link and clears the preview. The two-click flow now also shows the elastic line while a start node is pending. Escape cancels. design_lint.sh passes with no new colour, stroke or frame literals. validation/canvas_perf/run_canvas_bench.sh shows no per-frame regression.
tasks.risk: Publishing pendingLinkPoint on every drag frame adds one editor publish per frame — route it through the onContinuousHover path, which is already throttled. The node's DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0) and the canvas-level drag both fire; verify the .node origin early-return still holds.

tasks.title: Fix the corner resize grip, which is misplaced whenever the Results pane is visible
tasks.rationale: The Results pane force-shows itself after the first solver run and then persists, so this is the common state, not the edge case. VERIFIED: CornerResizeOverlay.swift:91 computes `dividerY = outer.arrangedSubviews[0].frame.height` — the TOP row's height — and CornerResizeOverlay.swift:112-122 then places the bottom.terminal.ai grip at that same y, although with Results present the bottom row starts at top.height + divider + results.height. The outer split's arranged subviews are [top, results, bottom] (VERIFIED at ContentView.swift:49-55). Dragging the grip therefore jumps two unrelated dividers, and there is no grip at the results|bottom junction at all.
tasks.implementation: Give CornerSpot an explicit `outerDividerIndex: Int` and compute each junction's y from the accumulated heights of the outer split's arranged subviews rather than always `arrangedSubviews[0].frame.height`. This needs NO ContentView change: derive the bottom row as the LAST arranged subview, so its top edge is `sum(heights of all but the last) + (count-1) * outer.dividerThickness`. The two TopHSplit grips anchor to outer divider index 0; the terminal|ai grip anchors to `outer.arrangedSubviews.count - 2`. Thread the index through `currentOuterY` and `moveDividers` (CornerResizeOverlay.swift:202, 214-216) instead of the hard-coded `ofDividerAt: 0`.

With Results hidden, behaviour is byte-identical to today. Verify by reading arranged-subview frames at runtime or by screenshot comparison.

tasks.title: Escape cancels an in-flight drag; arrow keys pan when nothing is selected
tasks.rationale: Two small gestures every dragging/scrolling surface has. VERIFIED: NetworkCanvasScrollContainer.swift:628-631 routes all four arrow key codes to nudgeSelection unconditionally and never calls super.keyDown, while nudgeSelection returns early on an empty selection (NetworkEditorModel.swift:1803-1806) — so with nothing selected an arrow key does absolutely nothing and does not fall through the responder chain either. And Escape (:606-610) maps to deselectAll, which does not touch dragStartPositions, dragNodeID or the open beginMutation group held in CanvasContentView's @State (NetworkCanvasView.swift:168-176, 493).

tasks.rationale: For a tool whose document is a routing graph, this is the single most damaging defect present. VERIFIED: `deleteSelection()` computes `currentSelectionIDs()` — nodes only (NetworkEditorModel.swift:697-701) — and guards `!ids.isEmpty`, so a link-only selection returns immediately (NetworkEditorModel.swift:680-682). Meanwhile QnetCommands.swift:147 defines `hasSelection = hasNodeSelection || editor.selectedLinkID != nil`, so the Edit ▸ Delete menu item is ENABLED in exactly that state — a dead command with no feedback. tasks.implementation: In deleteSelection(): capture `selectedLinkID` alongside `ids`, change the guard to `guard !ids.isEmpty || selectedLinkID != nil else { return }`, and inside the existing performMutation block remove `links.removeAll { $0.id == linkID }` BEFORE the node removal. Name the undo step by what was removed — "Delete Link" / "Delete Node" / "Delete Selection" — so the Edit menu reads correctly. Make the status line say what was deleted, matching deleteLink's wording (:590-598). Leave `deleteLink(id:)` alone: the context menu and the VoiceOver action use it. tasks.title: Allow a station self-loop (the feedback arc the solvers already speak about)
tasks.rationale: Qnet is a queueing-network tool whose solvers, warnings and help text all speak about P[i][i] > 0, and whose renderer already draws a self-loop as a nested arc — but the Link tool flatly refuses to create one. VERIFIED: `if startID == nodeID { addStatus("Cannot link a node to itself."); return }` at NetworkEditorModel.swift:1982-1986. Rendering support already exists (CanvasGeometry.swift:343-370 LinkGeometry.selfLoop with `extraRadius` so multi-class loops nest, dispatched at :1059-1061 on fromNodeID == toNodeID). Export and diagnostics already handle them (QnetGUIApp.swift:6566-6569 lists self-loop stations, :7053 reports max P[i][i], :6807 handles P[i][i] ≥ 1) and CanvasImageExport.swift:131 already pads for a self-loop chip. The AI path has no such guard (:2124-2148), so the two entry points already disagree.

Route the allowed case through the existing class-selection logic immediately below it (candidateClasses / usedClasses / chosenClass) so a multi-class self-loop picks a free class exactly as a normal link does, and preserve the chain-continuation behaviour. A second click on the SAME node is how the user expresses it and conflicts with nothing else in the addLink flow. BEFORE shipping, check for an infinite loop or singular matrix at P[i][i] → 1 in the traffic-equation solve behind refreshStationUtilisation (:1645-1668); the FlagBar feedback classifier already has a self-loop branch (:210-235).

tasks.title: Stop every hand-built network being born exactly unstable
tasks.rationale: VERIFIED: NetworkNode's default init uses `QueueDistribution.exponential.defaultParameters` (Models.swift:379, :879) which is `"rate=1.0"` (:207), and addNode constructs a node with all defaults (NetworkEditorModel.swift:2106). AnalyticalTractability short-circuits to unstable(), networkWarnings emits "station 1 is overloaded", and the Inspector paints ρ in danger ink. The bundled examples all use λ = 1.0 with μ = 1.1111111 (ρ = 0.9) and RandomNetworkGenerator defaults to targetRho 0.9 precisely because that is the useful regime.
tasks.implementation: In addNode (NetworkEditorModel.swift:2083-2113), construct a STATION with distributionParameters "rate=1.1111111" (μ = λ/0.9), leaving NetworkNode's own init defaults alone so no saved document changes meaning. Also make a SOURCE arrive as .poisson with "lambda=1.0" rather than .exponential, matching every bundled example and what MethodAdvisor's sourcesArePoisson test looks for. State the resulting ρ in the status line addNode already emits ("Added station S1 — ρ = 0.900 against the default source rate") so the number is taught rather than merely defaulted.

tasks.title: Guard sendCommand against a busy or non-prompt shell
tasks.rationale: Every solver launch is TYPED INTO the interactive shell. In runScript (VERIFIED at QnetGUIApp.swift:5799: `} 2>&1 | tee "\(handle.outputPath)"` followed by `_rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}`) and in silentScript (:7474, same shape), change to `} 2>&1 | tee "<outputPath>" | <numberFilter>` — appending a SECOND pipe stage, never wrapping the brace group, so `${PIPESTATUS[0]}` keeps pointing at the brace group and every exit code is unchanged. Emit the filter from a new `private func outputPrecisionFilter(decimals:) -> String` as a perl one-liner (perl is already an unconditional dependency of the wrapper, :5791). Requirements: (1) UNBUFFERED AND CR-AWARE — `$|=1`, read fixed-size chunks, split on /(?<=[\r\n])/, flush each record; a line-oriented awk/sed filter would swallow every intermediate frame of withProgress/withSpinner (:5614-5745 write `\r`-terminated frames with no newline until the end) and destroy the progress UI. This is the single biggest implementation risk. (2) Pass through VERBATIM any line matching /^QNET_[A-Z_]+_V1\b/ — QNET_QBD_METRIC_V1, QNET_NODE_METRIC_V1, QNET_MLMC_STATUS_V1, QNET_METHOD_FAILURE_V1, QNET_COMPARISON_STATUS_V1, QNET_SBD_STATUS_V1 — because rounding them corrupts stored results and breaks ResultOutputParser's integer-only regexes. (3) Skip ANSI escape runs /\e\[[0-?]*[ -\/]*[@-~]/. (4) Rewrite only tokens matching /(?<![\w.])[+-]?(?:\d+\.\d+|\.\d+)(?:[eE][+-]?\d+)?(?![\w.])/ — numbers that ALREADY carry a decimal point — so bare integers (counts, station indices, seeds, iteration counts, exit codes, caps) are untouched by construction, and the look-around keeps `S1.2`, version `0.90.34` and `/tmp/BNET_run_3.4.sh` out. (5) Magnitude policy: v == 0 or |v| ≥ 10^-decimals → `%.<d>f`, else `%.<max(1,d-1)>e`; normalize `-0.000…` to positive. VERIFIED necessary: `awk 'function f(v){return sprintf("%.3f",v+0)} BEGIN{print f("1.5e-08"); print f("-0.0001")}'` prints `0.000` and `-0.000` today. (6) Rewrite in place padded/trimmed to the ORIGINAL token width so pre-aligned tables (lpSummaryAwk %-16.4f, MLMC %10.4f, showNetworkPrimitives %10.5f) do not shear. Keep buildComparisonAwk's fmt7 on the same decimals so the awk tables are idempotent under the filter, and apply the same magnitude policy inside fmt7 AND fmtv together (fmtv's delta compares values rounded to N decimals, so if fmt7 switches to scientific the delta's rounding must switch with it).
